newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican banks close down in protest at robberies.
newsitem.headline: Mexican banks close down in protest at robberies.

text.p: Thousands of Mexicans in northern Chihuahua state faced a weekend without cash after banks closed in protest over a spate of robberies.

All banks in Chihuahua shut for an hour on Thursday in a protest over lack of protection, while in Ciudad Jimenez they closed all day, sources said, leaving many of the town's 80,000 residents without access to money until Monday because of a national holiday on Friday.
Chihuahua has been hit by 16 bank robberies this year on top of 49 last year. The northern cattle ranching state has only 250 bank branches.
The lockout followed a robbery on March 15 in Ciudad Jimenez when policemen guarding the bank turned into robbers, shot and killed the 25-year-old manager and injured a cashier.
"It was the straw that broke the camel's back," Ricardo Duran Armendariz, the treasurer of the Chihuahua Banking Center, told local media.
Friday is a Mexican national holiday to honor 19th century president Benito Juarez. Banks and financial markets are closed.
"Most cash machines are also out of service," local newspaper reporter Jorge Montes de Oca told Reuters.
Crime has risen in Mexico since the 1994 peso devaluation and ensuing recession left thousands without work. The number of bank robberies has skyrocketed nationally.
